proof:
Source: parent proof steps 3(a), 3(b); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 and Lemma 3.9 (push-forward of integer multiplicity currents; chapter-06.txt lines 405–418 and 770–862), applied to the inverse similarity η⁻¹.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
1. Let x' := −λ⁻¹x, λ' := λ⁻¹ > 0 and κ := η_{x',λ'}. Then κ(z) = −λ'⁻¹x' + λ'⁻¹z = −λ·(−λ⁻¹x) + λz = x + λz = ι(z). Since η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y, we get η∘κ = id and κ∘η = id, and V := κ(η(U)) = U (every u ∈ U equals κ(η(u)), and κ(η(u)) = u for u ∈ U).
2. Definition of S''. Let S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)). The blow-up κ_#S' := η_{x',λ'#}S' is a current in κ(η(U)) = V. Since U ⊆ V (step 1), define S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) by S''(ω') := κ_#S'(ω') for ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where ω' is regarded as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(V) with the same underlying form (restriction of the domain, SimonGMT restrictDomain, which preserves linearity and sequential continuity).
3. η_#S'' = S'. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). By testform_correspondence (a) (for U, x, λ) choose ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; by testform_correspondence (c), η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}S''(ω') = λ^{−n}κ_#S'(ω'). Now apply testform_correspondence (c) to the domain η(U), the current S', the point x' and λ' > 0, the test form ω' regarded in 𝒟ⁿ(κ(η(U))) and the test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)): its hypothesis ω(z) = ω'(κ(z)) for all z holds because ω'(κ(z)) = ω(η(κ(z))) = ω(z). Hence κ_#S'(ω') = λ'^{−n}S'(ω) = λⁿS'(ω), and η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}λⁿS'(ω) = S'(ω). As ω was arbitrary, η_{x,λ#}S'' = S'.
4. Integer multiplicity. Suppose S' is integer multiplicity, represented by an IMRep R₁ in η(U). By rep_pushforward (applied to the set η(U), the current S', the point x', λ' > 0 and R₁) there is an IMRep R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) in κ(η(U)) = V representing κ_#S'. Since V = U, the same data form an IMRep in U: M₂ ⊆ V = U, every compact K ⊆ U satisfies K ⊆ V so the local integrability condition transfers, and the remaining conditions do not involve the domain. This IMRep represents S'': for ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), S''(ω') = κ_#S'(ω') = R₂.action(ω'), the action depending only on the underlying form. Hence S'' is integer multiplicity. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build from the two siblings' exact types): take S'' := (blowUp S' (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr hlam).ne').restrictDomain hUV with hUV : U ⊆ dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' (dilation x λ '' U) obtained from hdom : dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' (dilation x λ '' U) = U (image_image); prove η_#S'' = S' by GeometricCurrentOn.ext, the sibling's evaluation formula twice, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, testFormOnInclusion_coe, inv_inv, mul_pow, inv_mul_cancel₀; the IMRep in U is ⟨R₂.carrier, R₂.mult, R₂.orient, R₂.measurableSet_carrier, R₂.carrier_subset.trans hdom.subset, R₂.rectifiable, R₂.measurable_mult, R₂.mult_pos, fun K hK hKU => R₂.locallyIntegrable_mult K hK (hKU.trans hUV), R₂.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, R₂.orients⟩, representing S'' by fun ω => hR₂ (testFormOnInclusion hUV n ω).
key_steps: The inverse of η is the dilation κ = η_{−λ⁻¹x, λ⁻¹}, so κ(η(U)) = U.
S'' := κ_#S' restricted to U; two applications of testform_correspondence (c) give η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}λⁿS'(ω) = S'(ω).
If S' is integer multiplicity, rep_pushforward for κ gives an IMRep of κ_#S' in κ(η(U)) = U, which represents S''.
